messages:
leo: Noticed p99 for /v1/reply spike during the canary. p50 looks fine but p99 went from ~120ms to ~820ms. Dashboard shows two variant routes (v1 / v1-quant) each with tiny sample counts. Link: https://redwood.internal/s/reply-canary
maya: Are we splitting samples across model variants for the canary? If traffic is 90/10 we might get very few samples in the small cohort.
frank: Yes, routing policy sent ~8% traffic to v1-quant. Console shows per-variant sample_count: v1=240, v1-quant=11 in the minute bucket. That small cohort dominates the p99 when we surface per-endpoint percentiles.
sre-kim: Can you paste the raw for the small cohort? Want to see distribution vs sketch.
frank: raw dump for v1-quant:
```
window: 2026-04-20T14:06Z
endpoint: /v1/reply (variant=v1-quant)
sample_count: 11
latencies_ms: [22,24,25,27,30,32,34,36,310,330,340]
tdigest_p99: 340
```
maya: With n=11 p99 is basically one of the top samples. If the UI by default shows per-variant percentiles that will confuse product folks who look at /v1/reply overall and expect stable numbers.
leo: Right now console shows two lines (v1 and v1-quant) and a combined aggregate that is computed by rollup. But our rollup picks the highest-variance path by default when users expand details which is misleading. We should make provenance explicit.
product-zoe: UX idea: when routing splits exist, show an aggregated percentile plus a per-variant breakdown. For small per-variant samples, add a "split-samples" badge: "small cohort - percentile unstable (n=11)" and explain that the cohort is a routing slice. Also provide an "aggregate by endpoint" toggle that computes combined percentile across variants.
maya: Implementation note: combined-percentile across variants can be approximated by merging tdigest sketches server-side before rendering, but we need to flag when variants use different rollup modes (sketch vs histogram vs raw). Show provenance string like "merged:tdigest (sketchs=2)".
sre-kim: For alerts: do not fire p99 SLOs based on per-variant percentiles when variant sample_count < 30. Alerts should evaluate on the rollup-aggregate unless the SLO is variant-specific.
frank: Also suggest console default: hide per-variant percentile if variant sample_count < 20 and instead show a single line with combined percentile and a disclosure link.
leo: Another ops-friendly option: surface both the merged percentile and the max-variant percentile (labeled "peak cohort"), so SREs can decide if the spike is localized. E.g., p99: 150ms (merged) | peak cohort: 340ms (v1-quant, n=11).
product-zoe: Love that. UX should show small chart with both series and a confidence chip (high/med/low) based on combined sample_count and largest-variant-sample. Proposed thresholds: combined < 50 -> low, combined 50-300 -> medium, >300 -> high.
maya: For smoothing: when routing weights change we should avoid carrying previous high-weight variant stats into a newly small cohort. If variant sample_count < 50, reset smoothing for that variant for the first 2 windows after weight change.
sre-kim: Ops action: We'll silence p99 alerts for that canary window and annotate the rollout note that this is a routing-split artifact. For long-term, alert engine change: gate per-variant percentile alerts on sample_count >= 30.
devex-bot: action created: ENG-PLAT-1701 "Routing-split percentile UX + alert gating" assigned to maya + frank, due 2026-04-15.
leo: I'll add a short blurb to the canary postmortem that endpoint p99 spikes can be caused by small-traffic cohorts due to routing policies and that console will be updated to make this explicit.
product-zoe: I'll add guidance in the rollout playbook: when canarying variants, prefer median-based SLOs or use weighted aggregate percentiles for low-traffic cohorts.
frank: I'll prototype merged-sketch server endpoint to return merged tdigest plus provenance flags; UI will lazy-fetch per-variant raw samples on click.
maya: I'll draft the UI copy and the badge designs tomorrow and post in #eng-platform.
sre-kim: Thanks team. I'll update alert rules and close the noisy canary alert.
